findings.issue: The app ships with zero tests of its own: no test runner, no test script, no test files, despite ~660 significant LOC of data-transformation logic.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (or SvelteKit's experimental vitest integration) and start with unit tests for the pure helpers in src/lib/utils.js, which are dependency-free and cover spec-critical formatting rules.

findings.issue: Home-page filtering, 48-per-page pagination, page clamping and URL param construction/omission are untested; this is the most refactor-prone code in the app and leans on the non-obvious page.shallow?.url contract (line 12).
findings.suggestion: Extract filtering/pagination into a testable module and add tests for slice bounds, ?page out-of-range/NaN, filter-changes-reset-to-page-1, and default-param omission.

findings.issue: The sort comparator handles nulls-last before applying direction, numeric vs localeCompare string comparison, and relies on stable sort over pre-sorted rows for ties — three easy things to break with no test to catch it.
findings.suggestion: Extract the comparator to a pure function and test: descending sort with missing values, numeric columns containing nulls, tie stability, and aria-sort state after toggle.

findings.issue: The search debounce timer is never cleared on component destroy; typing then immediately clicking a card fires goto('/?q=…') ~150 ms later from the Pokémon page, corrupting history or throwing on a shallow cross-route goto. No test would catch this.
findings.suggestion: Clear the timer in an $effect cleanup or onDestroy, and add a test that navigates immediately after typing.

findings.issue: The Pokémon page's data assembly is dense and untested: default game = highest order (games.at(-1)), fixed-then-alphabetical method ordering, stat label mapping and total, recursive evolution-tree building.
findings.suggestion: Add unit/integration tests for the load function using a small fixture (e.g. Deoxys default-variety mapping and an Eevee-style branching chain).

findings.issue: speciesCardsFromRefs encodes three spec rules — exclude ids >= 10000, dedupe by id, map Pokémon to species — with boundary behaviour no test guards.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with refs covering id 9999 vs 10000, duplicates, and deoxys-normal → deoxys mapping.

findings.issue: The HTTP client's error semantics are untested: 404 resolves to cached null, non-2xx throws, failed requests are evicted only if the cache still holds the same promise. A regression here turns not-found pages into 500s or serves poisoned cache.
findings.suggestion: Unit test get() against a stubbed fetch for 404, 500, and retry-after-network-failure cases.

findings.issue: Error and not-found rendering (error(404) in four load functions, plus the excluded-type 404 in types/[name]/+page.server.js:19) has no coverage beyond the acceptance suite's not-found URL checks.
findings.suggestion: Add a test that a thrown non-Kit error in a load still renders a sane page rather than an unstyled 500.

findings.issue: sortKey/sortDir persist across game changes (component keyed by method.key, rows replaced), so a user's sort silently re-applies to a new table; untested and unspecified behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Decide and test the intended behaviour (reset sort when rows change, or document the carry-over).

summary: The app is competently written against current SvelteKit 3 / Svelte 5 practice, but it contains no tests of its own — no runner, no script, no cases — so every risk area (filtering, pagination, URL state, sorting, alternate-form exclusion, API error handling) is guarded only by the harness's acceptance suite. The pure helpers in utils.js and the MovesTable comparator are the cheapest high-value places to start. Until then, any refactor of the data layer can silently break spec-critical behaviour with nothing failing in CI.
